transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12 20:30 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO - Lumos Health), Maya Santos (Head of ML Ops - Lumos), Daniel Park (Security)
Shared links: https://redwood-demo/console-tour (deck), security-docs.redwood/v1 (sec pack)

Summary (auto): quick console tour, focus on per-route cost insights, discuss pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our SE. today we'll do a quick console walkthrough focusing on the usage analytics, per-route dashboards and the cost breakdowns you asked about.
[00:22] Jordan Lee: cool, thanks Alex. we've got Maya from ML Ops and Daniel from security on. we mostly want to see how we'd measure cost per feature — our billing team wants line item cost by route.
[00:35] Priya Patel: yeah totally, that's a common ask. i'll share my screen and jump into the console. bear with me, small delay.
[01:05] Speaker 2 (Priya?): opening the usage analytics page. top-level view shows tokens, requests, p50/p95 latency and cost estimate. note this is cost-estimate, tied to model profile + quantization. you can filter by model, route, time range.
[01:35] Maya Santos: can we group by route? we have ~30 routes (search, summarization, triage, clinical extraction). need to tag them for business units.
[01:50] Priya Patel: yep — routes map to API keys or route names. you can set metadata tags and then use the per-route dashboard. i'll open a route example — "summarize-encounters".
[02:25] Priya Patel: here you can see requests over time, token histogram, average tokens per request, and cost-per-1000-requests. the cost column breaks down model compute, batching efficiency, and prefix caching savings.
[03:00] Jordan Lee: interesting — what's batching efficiency?
[03:08] Priya Patel: that's our measured improvement from continuous batching. for example, when we batch small short requests the per-token overhead drops. the console shows an "effective throughput" metric and gives suggestions like "enable 50ms batching window".
[03:35] Daniel Park: how accurate are these estimates? security will want deterministic numbers for budgeting and audits.
[03:45] Alex Chen: the estimates use model perf profiles plus recent real traffic. for Dedicated customers you can pin capacity and get invoice-grade reports. for hosted the console uses estimated unit prices — we do have downloadable CSV reports you can attach to internal billing.
[04:10] Maya Santos: we also want to see per-model and per-quantization breakdown. we sometimes run gpt-like base and then 4-bit quant variants.
[04:25] Priya Patel: absolutely — each route can be mapped to a model variant. the cost view shows model flavor, quantization (e.g., fp16 vs int4) and expected latency differences. there's a toggle to show hypothetical cost if we switch to a quantized variant, good for tradeoff analysis.
[04:50] Speaker 1 (Jordan): ok show me the compare view.
[05:05] Priya Patel: switching to compare, selecting summarize-encounters: baseline uses model-x-fp16, alt is model-x-int4; we predict ~45% cost reduction with a 12-18% latency increase on p95, depending on sequence length. console also warns of potential quality regressions and links to eval sets.
[05:40] Jordan Lee: hmm quality regression is a hard limit for clinical text. we need to run evals on our test prompts.
[05:50] Priya Patel: yes we can attach your prompt set — Redwood Optimize integration will run A/B quality checks and alert on regressions.
[06:10] Daniel Park: switching to security, if we wanted VPC/private deployment, can the console still show these dashboards?
[06:22] Alex Chen: yes — Private and Dedicated both send metrics to the control plane; in VPC we provide a private control plane option or you can host metrics in your cluster. audit logs and request IDs are available, and all telemetry can be pushed to your SIEM.
[06:45] Daniel Park: KMS integration? we need CMEK for model keys and data-at-rest.
[06:52] Priya Patel: we support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Key usage is logged in the audit trail. we'll share the KMS integration guide after the call.
[07:10] Maya Santos: great. also curious about per-route cost allocation — do you have per-team chargeback exports?
[07:20] Priya Patel: yes you can export by tag and route; there's a chargeback CSV export that includes token counts, model cost, routing tier cost, and caching impact per route.
[07:40] Alex Chen: one thing to call out: our routing policies can route by latency SLO or cost. so less critical paths can route to cheaper model variants or fallback to cached responses. the console shows the actual routing decisions and the savings attributed to those policies.
[08:05] Jordan Lee: can we simulate traffic to see impact if we flip a route to cheaper variant?
[08:12] Priya Patel: yep — there's a simulation tab. you provide baseline traffic, pick a policy, and it projects cost and latency changes. it's probabilistic, but useful for planning.
[08:35] Speaker 3 (Maya): are there internal examples?
[08:40] Priya Patel: i brought a sample we use with retailers — you can see a per-route dashboard for search vs personalization, and the cost delta when moving to int4.
[09:05] Alex Chen: i'll also note our Console has per-token heatmaps and route-level p95 latency panels; customers use them to set SLOs and detect regressions quickly.
[09:30] Jordan Lee: on billing cadence — do you bill by token only or also a routing/throughput surcharge?
[09:40] Alex Chen: hosted is usage-based by tokens + request units; Dedicated has reserved capacity pricing plus overage and optional routing tiers for high-availability. we'll provide a pricing sheet in the follow-up.
[10:00] Daniel Park: compliance question — can audit logs include original request IDs and who accessed the console? we need RBAC and SSO.
[10:12] Priya Patel: yes, RBAC with SAML SSO, and audit logs list user activity. we can scope what fields are logged for privacy.
[10:35] Maya Santos: do you store prompt data in hosted? what's retention?
[10:40] Alex Chen: hosted retains logs for 30 days by default, configurable with add-ons. Private deployments keep logs per your policy. we can redact PII on ingest if you need.
[11:05] Jordan Lee: curious about automatic batching/caching instrumentation — you mentioned prefix/KV cache earlier?
[11:12] Priya Patel: yes, Redwood does prefix caching and KV cache that caches previous context for repeated queries. console surfaces hit-rate, saving-per-route, and you can tune window sizes. sometimes transcription shows K-V cache as "KV cash" in older exports, haha.
[11:40] Jordan Lee: nice. that could shave a lot off for repeat queries in triage.
[11:52] Maya Santos: on the artifacts you mentioned — can you share the security pack and the demo tenant?
[11:58] Alex Chen: for sure. i'll send the security-pack link and sample pilot agreement after this call. Priya will set up a demo tenant with example dashboards.
[12:15] Priya Patel: quick note on the per-route tags: once you tag, the console groups and you can apply custom cost-allocation rules, e.g., 60/40 split for shared routes.
[12:35] Jordan Lee: good — also we want automated alerts when cost spikes above threshold for a route.
[12:42] Priya Patel: alerting is there — email/Slack/webhook. you can set budget alerts by route or team.
[13:00] Alex Chen: ok let's move to questions — any blockers to running a pilot?
[13:05] Maya Santos: main blocker is security clearance — Daniel needs the SOC2 scope and KMS details. also we need a short runbook for onboarding.
[13:20] Daniel Park: yes and a legal review; we may want a DPA with specific data residency clauses.
[13:30] Alex Chen: understood. we'll include SOC2 artifacts and DPA template in the follow-up.
[13:45] Jordan Lee: timeline — we'd like to start a pilot in two weeks and run for 3 weeks.
[13:52] Alex Chen: sounds doable; we'll aim to get the pilot agreement and demo tenant ready in 48 hours and then schedule the benchmark run.
[14:05] Priya Patel: i'll note down the routes Maya will send and set up a compare test with Dedicated capacity so we can measure p95 under load.
[14:25] Speaker 1 (Jordan): any other notes?
[14:30] Alex Chen: recap — Alex send pricing and pilot agreement; Priya provision demo tenant and run initial compare; Maya share traffic and prompt eval; Daniel send SOC2 questions. we'll tentatively schedule benchmark week of 2026-10-19.
[14:55] Jordan Lee: thanks all, that covers it.
[15:00] Alex Chen: thanks — end call.

End of transcript.
